claims.source: Joint federal statement, 17 December 2024, reported by The Debrief
claims.text: Joint statement of 17 December 2024 by DoD, DHS, FBI and FAA: 'We have not identified anything anomalous, and do not assess the activity to date to present a national security or public safety risk over the civilian airspace in New Jersey or other states.'

The FBI received over 5,000 drone reports; officials analysed roughly 100 specific leads and attributed them to commercial, hobbyist and law enforcement drones, manned aircraft, helicopters and stars.
The assessment acknowledged limited recent sightings over military facilities in restricted airspace, contradicting earlier White House statements denying such incidents.
Wright-Patterson Air Force Base closed its airspace for nearly four hours on 14-15 December 2024 due to unauthorized drone activity.

of.label: New Jersey and East Coast Drone Wave (Nov-Dec 2024)

sources.name: The Debrief - Pentagon says mystery drones are common UAS and misidentifications

desc: From mid-November into December 2024 a wave of nocturnal drone sightings over New Jersey and neighbouring states produced more than 5,000 reports to the FBI and a political crisis. On 17 December 2024 the Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security, FBI and FAA issued a joint statement: 'We have not identified anything anomalous, and do not assess the activity to date to present a national security or public safety risk over the civilian airspace in New Jersey or other states.' Officials said they had run down about 100 specific leads and found 'commercial drones, hobbyist drones, and law enforcement drones, as well as manned fixed-wing aircraft, helicopters, and stars mistakenly reported as drones.' Two features make this a coverup-strand item rather than a debunking. First, the same assessment conceded 'limited' sightings over military facilities in restricted airspace, contradicting earlier White House statements that there had been none. Second, it landed while Wright-Patterson Air Force Base had closed its airspace for nearly four hours on 14-15 December over unauthorized drone activity. A four-agency statement that resolves 100 of 5,000 reports and generalises the result to all of them is not an investigation finding; it is a communications posture, and it is recorded here as one.
